varieties.name: Peppermint
varieties.description: Peppermint is a popular and aromatic mint variety known for its strong, refreshing flavor. This perennial herb has dark green leaves with a hint of purple and is widely used in culinary applications, teas, and aromatherapy. Peppermint's invigorating scent and taste make it a versatile and beloved addition to herb gardens.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong, cooling menthol flavor with refreshing, sharp peppery notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, slightly fuzzy leaves with serrated edges

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Peppermint is a natural hybrid of spearmint and watermint, known for its strong menthol flavor.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Peppermint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support healthy growth. Prune regularly to prevent leggy growth and encourage bushiness. Harvest leaves for culinary and aromatic use. WARNING: Mint spreads aggressively - consider growing in containers or using root barriers!

varieties.name: Spearmint
varieties.description: Spearmint is a classic mint variety known for its mild and sweet flavor. This perennial herb has bright green, serrated leaves and is widely used in culinary applications, beverages, and medicinal preparations. Spearmint's refreshing taste makes it a popular choice for both culinary and aromatic uses.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Bright, crinkled leaves with prominent veins and serrated edges

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Spearmint has been used for centuries in traditional medicine for its potential digestive and respiratory benefits.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Spearmint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support healthy growth. Prune regularly to prevent leggy growth and encourage bushiness. Harvest leaves for culinary and aromatic use. WARNING: Mint spreads aggressively - consider growing in containers!

varieties.name: Chocolate Mint
varieties.description: Chocolate Mint is a delightful mint variety with a unique chocolatey flavor and aroma. This perennial herb features dark green leaves with a hint of purple and is a favorite for culinary uses, desserts, and aromatic purposes. Chocolate Mint adds a sweet and refreshing twist to various dishes and beverages.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Distinctive chocolate-mint combination with cool minty undertones and subtle cocoa notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, rounded leaves with serrated edges and purple-tinged stems

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Chocolate Mint is a natural hybrid of spearmint and peppermint, known for its distinctive chocolate flavor.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Chocolate Mint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support healthy growth. Prune regularly to prevent leggy growth and encourage bushiness. Harvest leaves for culinary and aromatic use. Best grown in containers to control spreading.

varieties.name: Apple Mint
varieties.description: Apple Mint, also known as Pineapple Mint, is a mint variety with a fruity and refreshing flavor. This perennial herb has bright green leaves and is popular for culinary uses, beverages, and garnishes. Apple Mint adds a delightful twist to salads, desserts, and drinks with its apple-like taste and aroma.

appearance.leaf_color: Bright Green, often with white variegation

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, fruity mint flavor with apple and pineapple notes - less menthol than other mints

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Soft, fuzzy, rounded leaves with woolly appearance

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Apple Mint gets its name from its fruity flavor, reminiscent of apples or pineapples.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Apple Mint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support healthy growth. Prune regularly to prevent leggy growth and encourage bushiness. Harvest leaves for culinary and aromatic use. Grows well in shadier spots than other mints.

varieties.name: Lemon Balm
varieties.description: Lemon Balm is a fragrant herb with a mild lemon scent and flavor. This perennial herb, also known as Melissa, is valued for its culinary uses, teas, and medicinal properties. Lemon Balm has bright green, heart-shaped leaves and is a delightful addition to herb gardens and relaxation blends.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - tolerates heat better than true mints

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Light, lemony citrus flavor with mild minty undertones - refreshing and uplifting

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Heart-shaped, deeply veined leaves with wrinkled texture

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Lemon Balm has been traditionally used to promote relaxation and improve mood, and is a member of the mint family.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Lemon Balm in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support healthy growth. Prune regularly to prevent leggy growth and encourage bushiness. Harvest leaves for culinary and aromatic use. Cut back before flowering to maintain best flavor.

varieties.name: Orange Mint
varieties.description: Orange Mint is a delightful mint variety that combines traditional mint flavor with bright citrus notes reminiscent of orange peel. This perennial herb features smooth, rounded leaves with a distinct orange fragrance and is excellent for both culinary and ornamental purposes. Orange Mint adds a unique citrusy-mint twist to beverages, desserts, and savory dishes, making it a versatile addition to any herb garden.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Refreshing mint with distinct orange citrus notes - sweeter and fruitier than peppermint

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, rounded leaves with slightly fuzzy texture

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Orange Mint's essential oils contain compounds similar to those found in orange peel, giving it an authentic citrus aroma that complements its minty freshness.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Orange Mint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support healthy growth. Prune regularly to maintain compact growth and prevent flowering. Best grown in containers to control aggressive spreading. Excellent for pairing with chocolate and fruit-based desserts.

varieties.name: Ginger Mint
varieties.description: Ginger Mint is a striking mint variety featuring bright yellow and green variegated foliage with a subtle ginger-mint flavor. This perennial herb is prized for its ornamental beauty and unique taste that combines traditional mint with hints of ginger spice. Ginger Mint adds both visual interest and culinary versatility to gardens, making it popular for decorative plantings, beverages, and Asian-inspired cuisine.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild mint flavor with subtle ginger-spice notes and fruity undertones

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, variegated leaves with serrated edges
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Medium - pleasant mint with ginger hints

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Ginger Mint's stunning variegation becomes more pronounced in bright light, making it one of the most ornamental mint varieties for container gardens and borders.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Ginger Mint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight for best variegation. Water regularly, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to maintain vibrant coloring. Prune regularly to encourage new variegated growth and prevent reversion to solid green. Excellent as an ornamental edging plant or container specimen.

varieties.name: Pineapple Mint
varieties.description: Pineapple Mint is a beautiful variegated mint variety with creamy white edges on its soft, fuzzy leaves and a delightful fruity flavor. This perennial herb combines ornamental appeal with culinary versatility, offering a mild mint taste with tropical pineapple notes. Less aggressive than many mint varieties, Pineapple Mint is perfect for containers, borders, and as a stunning edible garnish.

growth_info.growth_mode: Spreading via rhizomes (less aggressive than other mints)

appearance.leaf_color: Green with Creamy White Variegated Edges

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate to abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, fruity mint with sweet pineapple notes - very gentle and pleasant

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Soft, fuzzy, rounded leaves with woolly appearance and white margins

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Pineapple Mint is actually a variegated form of Apple Mint and is one of the most ornamental mints, often used in edible landscaping and flower arrangements.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Pineapple Mint in well-drained soil with partial sun to maintain best variegation (too much sun can scorch leaves). Water regularly, keeping soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks. Prune regularly to maintain variegation and remove any solid green shoots immediately. Less invasive than other mints but still benefits from container growing.

varieties.name: Mojito Mint
varieties.description: Mojito Mint, also known as Cuban Mint or Yerba Buena, is the authentic mint variety traditionally used in classic Cuban mojitos. This perennial herb features bright green leaves with a perfectly balanced mint flavor that's neither too strong nor too mild. With a smoother, less harsh taste than peppermint and more robust flavor than spearmint, Mojito Mint is the ideal choice for cocktails, beverages, and Caribbean cuisine.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering to keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest throughout growing season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - tolerates heat better than many mints

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Perfectly balanced mint flavor - smooth, refreshing, with citrus hints and no harsh aftertaste

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, bright leaves with slightly wrinkled texture and serrated edges

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Mojito Mint is specifically cultivated for its smooth, well-balanced flavor that doesn't overpower drinks, making it the preferred mint for professional bartenders worldwide.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Mojito Mint in well-drained soil with partial to full sunlight. Water regularly, keeping soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support vigorous growth. Prune regularly to encourage bushy growth and prevent flowering. Harvest frequently for best flavor. Excellent heat tolerance makes it ideal for warm-climate gardens.

varieties.name: Corsican Mint
varieties.description: Corsican Mint is a unique, miniature mint variety that forms a dense, moss-like ground cover with tiny, rounded leaves. This perennial herb releases a strong peppermint fragrance when walked upon, making it perfect for planting between stepping stones and in rock gardens. While primarily ornamental, Corsican Mint can be used sparingly in culinary applications and is prized for creating fragrant, low-maintenance ground cover in shady areas.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every six weeks with diluted fertilizer

tolerances.cold_tolerance: Moderate - may not survive harsh winters

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Intense peppermint flavor - very concentrated in tiny leaves

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Tiny, round leaves (2-4mm) creating moss-like carpet
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Very strong - intense peppermint scent when crushed

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Corsican Mint is one of the smallest mint species and can tolerate light foot traffic, releasing a wonderful peppermint fragrance when stepped on, making it perfect for scented pathways.

planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest dill leaves from late fall through spring. Dill bolts quickly in hot weather.

planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest dill leaves during the coolest months. Best grown as a winter annual in these zones.

varieties.name: Bouquet Dill
varieties.description: Bouquet Dill is a popular dill variety known for its feathery foliage and strong, aromatic flavor. This annual herb is commonly used in culinary applications, pickling, and as a garnish. With its upright growth habit and delicate leaves, Bouquet Dill is a versatile and flavorful addition to herb gardens and kitchen windowsills.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every six weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant leaves for 6-8 weeks, then large seed heads

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Low - bolts quickly in heat

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong, tangy anise-like flavor with fresh grassy notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Fine, feathery, thread-like leaves
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: Low - bolts readily in hot weather

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Bouquet Dill is named for its abundant and attractive flower heads, making it a favorite for both culinary and ornamental use.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Bouquet Dill seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight - dill has a taproot and doesn't transplant well. Water moderately, allowing the soil to dry slightly between watering. Fertilize every six weeks. Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest. Harvest leaves before flowering for best flavor.

varieties.name: Fernleaf Dill
varieties.description: Fernleaf Dill is a compact and dwarf dill variety known for its finely cut, fern-like foliage. This annual herb is prized for its culinary uses, especially in salads, sauces, and fish dishes. With its compact growth habit, Fernleaf Dill is suitable for small gardens, containers, and indoor herb gardens.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every six weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous leaf harvest from compact plants

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Low - bolts in heat

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, sweet dill flavor with delicate anise notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Very fine, densely packed feathery leaves
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: Moderate - slower to bolt than other varieties

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Fernleaf Dill is well-suited for compact spaces and container gardening due to its compact and attractive growth habit. It's also slower to bolt than standard dill.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Fernleaf Dill seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight - avoid transplanting. Water moderately, allowing the soil to dry slightly between watering. Fertilize every six weeks. Its compact size makes it perfect for containers and small spaces. Pinch back regularly to encourage bushiness.

varieties.name: Mammoth Dill
varieties.description: Mammoth Dill is a tall and vigorous dill variety known for its large, umbrella-like flower heads. This annual herb is valued for its culinary uses, especially in pickling and flavoring various dishes. With its robust growth habit, Mammoth Dill is a classic choice for larger herb gardens and farm plantings.

growth_info.recommended_container_size: Not recommended - too tall for containers

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant leaves and very large seed heads - excellent for pickling

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Low - bolts in heat

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong, bold dill flavor with pronounced anise notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Coarse, feathery leaves on tall stems

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Mammoth Dill is prized for its large and showy flower heads (up to 8 inches across), making it the go-to choice for pickling enthusiasts and large-scale herb production.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Mammoth Dill seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight - do not transplant. Space plants adequately as they grow very tall. May need staking in windy areas. Water moderately. This variety is best for garden beds rather than containers due to its height. Excellent for seed harvest.

varieties.name: Dukat Dill
varieties.description: Dukat Dill is a premium European variety known for its exceptional flavor and high essential oil content. This annual herb produces abundant, aromatic foliage with a sweeter, more refined taste than common dill varieties. Dukat is slower to bolt than most dill varieties, providing an extended harvest period. It's a favorite among chefs and serious gardeners for its superior culinary quality and productivity.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every six weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Extended abundant harvest of premium-quality leaves

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Medium - better heat tolerance than standard dill

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, refined dill flavor with rich anise notes - less bitter than common dill

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Fine, delicate feathery leaves - more tender than standard dill
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Very strong - highly aromatic with high oil content

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Dukat Dill contains up to 15% more essential oils than common dill varieties, giving it superior flavor and aroma, which is why it's the preferred choice in Scandinavian cuisine.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Dukat Dill seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight - avoid transplanting due to taproot. Water moderately, keeping soil evenly moist. Fertilize every six weeks. Its slow-bolting nature allows for extended harvest. Succession plant every 3-4 weeks for continuous supply. Harvest regularly to encourage more leaf production.

varieties.name: Long Island Mammoth
varieties.description: Long Island Mammoth Dill is a traditional American heirloom variety prized for its exceptional vigor and massive seed heads. This annual herb grows tall and strong, producing enormous flower umbels perfect for pickling cucumbers and making dill seed. A commercial favorite for over a century, Long Island Mammoth delivers abundant foliage and seeds, making it ideal for large-scale preservation and culinary use.

growth_info.recommended_container_size: Not recommended - too tall for containers

appearance.flower_color: Very large yellow umbrella-shaped clusters (8-10 inches wide)

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every six weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Extremely abundant leaves and massive seed heads

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Low - bolts in heat
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Medium - more drought tolerant than other varieties

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Classic, robust dill flavor with strong anise-caraway notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Coarse, substantial feathery leaves on thick stems

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Long Island Mammoth has been the standard commercial pickling dill in America since the early 1900s and can produce seed heads up to 10 inches across - perfect for canning whole cucumbers.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Long Island Mammoth seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight in a permanent location. Space generously as plants grow very large. Stake in windy areas to prevent toppling. Water moderately. Best suited for garden beds and commercial production. Allow plants to fully mature for maximum seed production.

varieties.name: Superdukat
varieties.description: Superdukat Dill is an improved strain of the popular Dukat variety, bred for even greater productivity and slower bolting. This annual herb combines exceptional flavor with remarkable heat tolerance and extended harvest period. Superdukat produces lush, dark blue-green foliage with intensely aromatic leaves that maintain their quality longer than standard varieties, making it a top choice for serious culinary enthusiasts and market gardeners.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every six weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Very abundant, extended harvest of premium leaves

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - excellent heat tolerance for a dill variety

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet, refined dill flavor with complex anise notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Fine, delicate, abundantly feathered leaves
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Very strong - extremely aromatic with very high oil content
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: Very High - among the slowest to bolt

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Superdukat was specifically bred to withstand warmer temperatures and extend the harvest season by several weeks compared to standard dill, making it ideal for summer growing in warm climates.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Superdukat seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight - do not transplant. Water moderately, maintaining even moisture. Fertilize every six weeks. Excellent for warm-season growing where other dills bolt quickly. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage continued production. Can be succession planted every 4 weeks.

varieties.name: Greensleeves
varieties.description: Greensleeves Dill is a unique slow-bolting variety bred specifically for extended leaf production. This annual herb maintains its vegetative growth much longer than traditional dill varieties, producing abundant feathery foliage over an extended period. With its compact, bushy habit and delayed flowering, Greensleeves is ideal for gardeners who want continuous fresh dill leaves without the quick transition to seed production.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Extended continuous leaf harvest over long period

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - excellent heat tolerance with delayed bolting

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Fresh, bright dill flavor with mild anise notes - sweeter than standard dill

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Fine to medium feathery leaves, dense and abundant
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: Very High - bred for extended vegetative growth

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Greensleeves can produce harvestable leaves for up to 10-12 weeks before flowering, compared to 6-8 weeks for standard dill varieties, making it perfect for fresh leaf production.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Greensleeves seeds directly in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water moderately, keeping soil evenly moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support extended leaf production. Harvest regularly to encourage bushier growth. Excellent for containers and intensive production. Less need for succession planting due to extended harvest period.

varieties.name: Tetra Dill
varieties.description: Tetra Dill is a specialized tetraploid variety with thicker stems, larger leaves, and more robust growth than standard diploid dill. This annual herb was developed through chromosome doubling, resulting in exceptionally vigorous plants with enhanced flavor and aroma. Tetra produces abundant, substantial foliage perfect for both fresh use and drying, making it a favorite for commercial herb production and serious home gardeners seeking maximum yield.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeding every four weeks with balanced fertilizer

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Very abundant harvest of large, flavorful leaves

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Medium - moderate heat tolerance
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Medium - more drought tolerant than standard dill

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Intense, concentrated dill flavor with powerful anise notes - very aromatic

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Coarse, substantial, thick feathery leaves on robust stems
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Extremely strong - very high essential oil content

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Tetra Dill's tetraploid genetics give it four sets of chromosomes instead of the normal two, resulting in larger cells, thicker stems, and up to 30% more essential oils than standard dill varieties.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Tetra Dill seeds directly in well-drained, fertile soil with full sunlight - requires more nutrients than standard dill. Water moderately and fertilize regularly every four weeks to support vigorous growth. Space plants adequately as they grow quite robust. Excellent for drying due to high oil content. Harvest regularly for best quality.

varieties.name: Common Sage
varieties.description: Common Sage, also known as Garden Sage, is a well-known and versatile herb with gray-green leaves and a distinct earthy flavor. This perennial herb is widely used in culinary applications, teas, and for its aromatic properties. Common Sage is known for its hardiness and can be a valuable addition to herb gardens and landscapes.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous harvest from established plants - best before flowering

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - thrives in hot, dry conditions
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - highly drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong, earthy, slightly peppery with piney, camphor-like notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Velvety, pebbly surface with soft gray-green leaves

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Common Sage has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties for over 2,000 years, and its Latin name 'Salvia' means 'to heal.'
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Common Sage in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing the soil to dry out between watering - overwatering is the most common cause of failure. Fertilize lightly once a month during the growing season. Prune regularly after flowering to maintain shape and prevent woodiness. Harvest leaves before flowering for best flavor.

varieties.name: Pineapple Sage
varieties.description: Pineapple Sage is a unique and aromatic sage variety with bright green leaves and a sweet pineapple fragrance. This perennial herb is valued for its culinary uses, teas, and ornamental appeal. Pineapple Sage is known for attracting pollinators with its vibrant red tubular flowers and is a delightful addition to herb gardens and landscape borders.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - prefers more moisture than common sage, keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant harvest of leaves and flowers throughout season

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - thrives in warm conditions
tolerances.cold_tolerance: Low - tender perennial, hardy only to zone 8
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Moderate - less drought tolerant than common sage

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, fruity pineapple flavor with mild sage undertones - refreshing and tropical

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, soft, bright green leaves with serrated edges

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Pineapple Sage is often used in both sweet and savory dishes, and its vibrant red flowers are edible and attract hummingbirds in late summer and fall!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Pineapple Sage in well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water moderately, keeping the soil more consistently moist than common sage. Fertilize once a month during the growing season. Prune regularly to maintain shape and encourage bushiness. Harvest leaves and flowers for culinary and ornamental use. In cold zones, grow as an annual or overwinter indoors.

varieties.name: Tricolor Sage
varieties.description: Tricolor Sage is a visually stunning sage variety with variegated leaves featuring shades of green, purple, and white. This perennial herb is not only prized for its ornamental appeal but also for its culinary uses. Tricolor Sage adds a burst of color to herb gardens and is an excellent choice for decorative containers.

appearance.leaf_color: Variegated - Green, Purple, White, and Pink

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - allow soil to dry between waterings, avoid overwatering
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate harvest - slower growing than common sage

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - less heat tolerant than common sage

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Similar to common sage but slightly milder - earthy with subtle peppery notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Velvety, variegated leaves with pink, purple, and white markings

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Tricolor Sage not only adds flavor to dishes but also serves as an attractive garnish due to its vibrant foliage. The variegation is most pronounced in cooler weather!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Tricolor Sage in well-drained soil with full sunlight (more sun intensifies the colors). Water moderately, allowing the soil to dry out between watering. Fertilize once a month during the growing season. Prune regularly to maintain compact shape and encourage colorful new growth. Harvest leaves for culinary and decorative use. May need winter protection in zone 6.

varieties.name: Purple Sage
varieties.description: Purple Sage is a striking ornamental and culinary herb featuring beautiful purple-gray foliage with a soft, velvety texture. This perennial subshrub combines the classic sage flavor with stunning visual appeal, making it equally valuable in the kitchen and garden. Purple Sage is slightly milder than common sage and is prized for its drought tolerance, aromatic leaves, and ability to add both flavor and color to culinary creations and landscape designs.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous harvest from established plants - best before flowering

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - thrives in hot, dry conditions
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - highly drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Earthy, slightly peppery sage flavor with subtle fruity notes - milder than common sage

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Velvety, soft purple-gray leaves with fuzzy surface

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Purple Sage's vibrant color deepens in cooler weather and full sun, and young leaves are often the most intensely purple before maturing to purple-gray.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Purple Sage in well-drained soil with full sunlight for best color development. Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month during growing season. Prune regularly after flowering to maintain compact shape and encourage new purple growth. Harvest young leaves for most intense color and flavor. Excellent for xeriscaping.

varieties.name: Golden Sage
varieties.description: Golden Sage is a beautiful variegated variety featuring bright green leaves with golden-yellow edges and splashes. This perennial herb offers the classic sage flavor while adding a bright, sunny accent to herb gardens and containers. Golden Sage is valued for its ornamental beauty, culinary uses, and ability to brighten shady corners of the garden with its luminous foliage.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - allow soil to dry between waterings, avoid overwatering
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate harvest - slower growing than common sage

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - less heat tolerant than common sage

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Classic sage flavor, slightly milder and sweeter than common sage

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Velvety, variegated leaves with golden-yellow margins

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Golden Sage's bright variegation can help illuminate darker areas of the garden, and the yellow coloring becomes more intense with adequate sunlight and cooler temperatures.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Golden Sage in well-drained soil with full sun to partial shade - some afternoon shade prevents leaf scorch in hot climates. Water moderately, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month. Prune regularly to maintain variegation and remove any solid green shoots immediately (they're more vigorous and will take over). Best color in spring and fall.

varieties.name: Berggarten Sage
varieties.description: Berggarten Sage is a German cultivar known for its large, rounded leaves and compact, non-flowering habit. This perennial herb produces broad, silvery-green foliage with exceptional flavor and minimal flowering, allowing for extended leaf production throughout the season. Berggarten is prized by chefs for its superior culinary quality and by gardeners for its attractive, low-maintenance growth habit.

appearance.flower_color: Rarely flowers - pale blue when it does

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant continuous harvest - produces more leaves due to minimal flowering

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - excellent heat tolerance
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - highly drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, robust sage flavor - slightly sweeter and less bitter than common sage

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Large, broad, rounded leaves with velvety silvery surface - nearly twice the size of common sage

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Berggarten Sage rarely produces flowers, which means it puts all its energy into producing large, flavorful leaves - making it one of the most productive culinary sages available!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Berggarten Sage in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month during growing season. Prune lightly to maintain shape - less pruning needed than common sage due to minimal flowering. Harvest large leaves regularly for culinary use. Excellent for zones with hot summers.

varieties.name: White Sage
varieties.description: White Sage, also known as Bee Sage, is a distinctive California native with striking silvery-white foliage and powerful aromatic properties. This perennial subshrub is sacred to many Indigenous peoples and is traditionally used for ceremonial smudging and spiritual practices. White Sage features intensely aromatic leaves covered in fine white hairs and produces tall spikes of white to pale lavender flowers that attract numerous pollinators.

appearance.flower_color: White to Pale Lavender on tall spikes

care_requirements.water_requirement: Very low - extremely drought tolerant, water sparingly only when established
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Minimal - light feeding once or twice during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate harvest - harvest sustainably for ceremonial use

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot, arid conditions
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Extremely High - native to arid climates

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very strong, pungent, camphor-like with eucalyptus notes - not typically used for culinary purposes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Thick, fleshy leaves densely covered with fine white hairs
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Extremely strong - powerfully aromatic and cleansing
herb_characteristics.culinary_strength: Not culinary - ceremonial and aromatic use only

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? White Sage has been used for centuries by Indigenous peoples of the Southwest for purification ceremonies, and it's important to harvest sustainably and respect its cultural significance.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant White Sage in extremely well-drained, sandy or gravelly soil with full sunlight. Water very sparingly - overwatering is fatal. Requires excellent drainage and low humidity. No fertilizer needed in native soils. Prune after flowering. Best suited for dry, Mediterranean climates or xeriscaping. Not recommended for humid regions. Harvest respectfully and sustainably.

varieties.name: Clary Sage
varieties.description: Clary Sage is a biennial or short-lived perennial herb known for its large, aromatic leaves and spectacular flower spikes with colorful bracts. This ornamental and medicinal sage produces impressive flowering displays in its second year, with pink, purple, or white bracts surrounding small flowers. Clary Sage has been traditionally used for its essential oils, medicinal properties, and as a flavoring agent, though it has a distinctly different flavor from culinary sage.

appearance.flower_color: Pink, Purple, or White bracts with small blue-white flowers

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - prefers consistent moisture but tolerates some drought
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding monthly during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant leaves in first year, spectacular flowers in second year

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - tolerates heat but prefers moderate climates
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Moderate - somewhat drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Bitter, musky flavor with floral notes - distinctly different from culinary sage, not recommended for cooking

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Large, wrinkled, heart-shaped leaves with hairy surface
herb_characteristics.culinary_strength: Not culinary - medicinal and aromatic use
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - biennial, flowers in second year

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Clary Sage essential oil is one of the most valuable sage oils in aromatherapy and perfumery, and the plant's name 'Clary' comes from 'clear eye,' referring to its traditional use for eye treatments.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Clary Sage in well-drained soil with full sun to partial shade. Water moderately, maintaining consistent moisture. Fertilize monthly during growing season. Forms leafy rosette first year, then produces spectacular flower spikes in second year. Deadhead spent flowers or allow to self-seed. Excellent for cottage gardens and pollinator plantings. Harvest leaves in first year, flowers in second year.

varieties.name: Tuscan Blue
varieties.description: Tuscan Blue Rosemary is a popular and aromatic rosemary variety with needle-like leaves and a robust, pine-like fragrance. This perennial herb is known for its culinary uses, especially in Mediterranean dishes, and its ornamental appeal. Tuscan Blue Rosemary is a versatile herb that adds flavor to various recipes and beauty to gardens.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant continuous harvest from established plants

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot, dry conditions
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - extremely drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong, pine-like flavor with camphor and eucalyptus notes - robust and aromatic

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Needle-like, dark green leaves with slightly rough texture
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Very strong - intensely aromatic and resinous

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Tuscan Blue Rosemary can grow 4-6 feet tall and is often used in roasts, stews, and grilled dishes, imparting a distinct Mediterranean flavor to the food.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Tuscan Blue Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing the soil to dry out between watering - overwatering is the main cause of death. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Prune regularly after flowering to maintain shape and prevent woodiness. Harvest sprigs year-round. In cold zones, grow in containers and overwinter indoors.

varieties.name: Arp
varieties.description: Arp Rosemary is a cold-hardy and aromatic rosemary variety with silvery-green leaves and a pine-like scent. This perennial herb is prized for its culinary uses, especially in roasts, marinades, and bread. Arp Rosemary is well-suited for various climates and is an excellent choice for both herb gardens and container planting.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant continuous harvest from established plants

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot conditions
tolerances.cold_tolerance: Very High - hardy to zone 6, one of the hardiest rosemary varieties
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - extremely drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild to medium pine flavor with lemon undertones - less intense than Tuscan Blue

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Needle-like, silvery gray-green leaves with soft texture
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Strong - aromatic with slight lemon notes

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Arp Rosemary is one of the cold-hardiest rosemary varieties and can withstand temperatures down to 10°F (-12°C), making it ideal for northern gardens!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Arp Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing the soil to dry out between watering. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Prune regularly to maintain shape and encourage bushiness. This variety is the best choice for cold climates - it can overwinter outdoors in zone 6 with mulch protection. Harvest sprigs year-round where hardy.

varieties.name: Barbecue Rosemary
varieties.description: Barbecue Rosemary is a robust and flavorful rosemary variety with dark green leaves and a strong aromatic profile. This perennial herb is specially bred for its culinary uses, particularly in grilling and barbecuing. Barbecue Rosemary adds a savory touch to meat and vegetable dishes, making it a favorite for outdoor cooking enthusiasts.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant continuous harvest - especially suited for large sprigs

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot conditions
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - extremely drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very strong, bold pine flavor with intense resinous notes - excellent for grilling

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Thick, sturdy needle-like leaves on strong stems - ideal for skewers
herb_characteristics.aroma_intensity: Very strong - intensely aromatic and pungent
herb_characteristics.culinary_strength: Very Strong - robust flavor for high-heat cooking

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Barbecue Rosemary is specifically bred for its robust flavor and sturdy stems, making it perfect for use as skewers for grilled kebabs - the stems impart flavor while cooking!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Barbecue Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing the soil to dry out between watering. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Prune regularly to maintain shape and encourage strong stem growth. Harvest mature woody stems for use as aromatic skewers, and fresh sprigs for marinades and rubs. Strip leaves from stems to create natural kebab skewers.

varieties.name: Prostrate Rosemary
varieties.description: Prostrate Rosemary, also known as Creeping Rosemary, is a low-growing, cascading variety with trailing stems that make it perfect for hanging baskets, containers, and ground cover. This perennial herb features the classic rosemary fragrance and flavor while offering unique ornamental value with its graceful, weeping habit. Prostrate Rosemary produces abundant pale blue flowers and is excellent for slopes, walls, and erosion control.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous harvest from cascading stems

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot, dry conditions
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - extremely drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Classic rosemary flavor - pine-like with mild camphor notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Needle-like, dark green leaves on trailing stems

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Prostrate Rosemary can cascade down walls and slopes, creating stunning living curtains of fragrant foliage, and is one of the most profuse bloomers among rosemary varieties!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Prostrate Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sunlight, ideally on slopes or in elevated containers. Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Prune to control spread and shape cascading growth. Excellent for hanging baskets where stems can trail freely. Harvest sprigs from trailing stems year-round in mild climates.

varieties.name: Blue Boy Rosemary
varieties.description: Blue Boy Rosemary is a compact, dwarf variety perfect for small gardens, containers, and edging. This perennial herb maintains a naturally rounded, bushy shape without extensive pruning and produces abundant bright blue flowers. Despite its diminutive size, Blue Boy offers full-strength rosemary flavor and fragrance, making it ideal for kitchen windowsills, small patios, and urban gardening where space is limited.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate continuous harvest from compact plants

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - tolerates hot conditions well

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Full-strength rosemary flavor - pine-like with sweet undertones

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Short, fine needle-like leaves, densely packed

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Blue Boy Rosemary is one of the smallest rosemary varieties, rarely exceeding 2 feet in height, making it perfect for those who want fresh rosemary but have limited space!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Blue Boy Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Minimal pruning needed - naturally maintains compact, rounded shape. Perfect for container growing and can be brought indoors for winter in cold climates. Excellent for windowsill herb gardens.

varieties.name: Miss Jessopp's Upright
varieties.description: Miss Jessopp's Upright Rosemary is a vigorous, strongly upright variety known for its tall, columnar growth habit and excellent culinary quality. This perennial herb produces abundant pale blue flowers and maintains a narrow, vertical form without extensive training. Named after a Victorian gardener, Miss Jessopp's Upright is prized for its strong flavor, cold hardiness, and architectural presence in the garden.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Very abundant continuous harvest from tall, productive plants

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot conditions
tolerances.cold_tolerance: High - hardy to zone 6-7 with protection
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - extremely drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong, classic rosemary flavor with intense pine and camphor notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Medium-length needle-like leaves on upright stems

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Miss Jessopp's Upright can grow 5-6 feet tall while remaining quite narrow, making it perfect for creating living hedges or vertical accents in the garden without taking up much horizontal space!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Miss Jessopp's Upright in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Prune to maintain desired height and shape - responds well to shaping. Excellent for creating rosemary hedges or topiaries. In zone 6, provide winter mulch protection and wind shelter.

varieties.name: Golden Rain Rosemary
varieties.description: Golden Rain Rosemary is a striking variegated variety featuring green needles streaked with golden-yellow, creating a bright, sunny appearance in the garden. This perennial herb offers the classic rosemary flavor while providing exceptional ornamental value with its colorful foliage. Golden Rain is particularly beautiful in spring when new growth emerges with the most intense golden coloration, making it a favorite for decorative containers and landscape accents.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - allow soil to dry between waterings, slightly less drought tolerant than green varieties
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate harvest - slower growing than solid green varieties

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - less heat tolerant than green varieties, benefits from afternoon shade in hot climates
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Moderate - less drought tolerant than solid green varieties

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Classic rosemary flavor - pine-like with mild camphor notes, similar to standard rosemary

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Needle-like leaves with golden-yellow streaks and variegation

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Golden Rain Rosemary's golden variegation is most pronounced in cooler weather and with adequate sunlight, and the plant may occasionally produce solid green shoots that should be pruned to maintain variegation!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Golden Rain Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sun to partial shade (afternoon shade in hot climates prevents leaf scorch). Water moderately, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize monthly to support variegated growth. Prune regularly and remove any solid green shoots immediately as they're more vigorous. Best golden color develops in spring and fall.

varieties.name: Salem Rosemary
varieties.description: Salem Rosemary is a cold-hardy, upright variety developed specifically for northern climates and challenging growing conditions. This perennial herb features pale blue flowers and good culinary quality while offering exceptional cold tolerance rivaling that of Arp. Salem maintains a neat, upright habit and produces abundant foliage with classic rosemary flavor, making it an excellent choice for gardeners in zones where most rosemary varieties struggle.

appearance.leaf_color: Medium to Dark Green needle-like leaves

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low - drought tolerant once established, allow soil to dry between waterings
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding once a month during growing season, or less

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Abundant continuous harvest from established plants

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot conditions
tolerances.cold_tolerance: Very High - hardy to zone 6, excellent cold tolerance
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Very High - extremely drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Medium to strong rosemary flavor - pine-like with balanced resinous notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Needle-like, medium green leaves with good texture

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Salem Rosemary was developed to withstand harsh winters and can survive temperatures down to 0°F (-18°C) with proper mulching, making it one of the best choices for northern gardeners!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Salem Rosemary in well-drained soil with full sunlight. Water sparingly, allowing soil to dry between waterings. Fertilize lightly once a month or less. Prune regularly to maintain shape and encourage bushiness. In zone 6, plant in protected location with good drainage and apply winter mulch. Can overwinter outdoors in most zone 6 locations with proper care. Excellent alternative to Arp for cold climates.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date, typically in mid to late March.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors after the danger of frost has passed, usually in late May to early June. Division of clumps can be done in spring.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Sow seeds directly outdoors in early spring (April-May) as soon as soil can be worked.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest chive leaves throughout the growing season. Cut leaves 2 inches above soil level for continuous harvest.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date, typically in early to mid-February.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors in April-May. Divide established clumps in spring or fall.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Sow seeds directly outdoors in early spring (March-April) as soon as soil can be worked.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest chive leaves from late spring through fall. Established plants can be harvested almost year-round in zone 6.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start seeds indoors in January-February, or divide established clumps in spring or fall.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors in March-April. Fall planting also works well.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Sow seeds directly outdoors in early spring (February-March) or fall (September-October).
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest chive leaves year-round in these zones. Chives are semi-evergreen and productive throughout the year.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start seeds indoors in fall/winter months when temperatures are cooler.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings or divide clumps during cooler months (October-January).
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Sow seeds directly outdoors during cooler months. Chives prefer cool weather and may struggle in extreme heat.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest chive leaves year-round. Best growth occurs during cooler months.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start seeds indoors during the coolest months of the year.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings or divide clumps during the coolest period (December-February).
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Sow seeds during the coolest months. Chives may struggle in tropical heat and are best grown as a cool-season annual.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest during cooler months when plants are most productive.

varieties.name: Common Chives
varieties.description: Common Chives, also known as Allium schoenoprasum, are a classic and versatile herb with slender, hollow leaves and a mild onion flavor. This perennial herb is popular in culinary applications, adding a fresh and subtle onion taste to a variety of dishes. Common Chives are easy to grow and are a staple in herb gardens and kitchen windowsills.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest - cut and come again

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler temperatures
tolerances.cold_tolerance: Very High - extremely hardy to zone 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, delicate onion flavor - fresh and subtle with slight sweetness

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Slender, hollow, cylindrical leaves (grass-like)
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, flowers are edible

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Common Chives belong to the Allium family, which includes onions, garlic, and leeks. The beautiful purple flowers are completely edible and make stunning garnishes!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Common Chives in well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water moderately, keeping the soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks during the growing season. Cut leaves 2 inches above soil level for continuous harvest. Divide clumps every 3-4 years to maintain vigor. The attractive purple flowers are edible - use as garnishes or in salads!

varieties.name: Garlic Chives
varieties.description: Garlic Chives, also known as Allium tuberosum or Chinese Chives, are a flavorful herb with flat, strap-like leaves and a distinct garlic taste. This perennial herb is widely used in culinary dishes, providing a mild garlic flavor without the intensity of fresh garlic. Garlic Chives are valued for their versatility and are a popular choice for both herb gardens and Asian cuisines.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous abundant harvest - very productive

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - more heat tolerant than common chives

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild garlic flavor with slight onion undertones - not as pungent as fresh garlic

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Flat, strap-like leaves (not hollow like common chives)
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, flowers are edible

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Garlic Chives are a staple in Chinese cuisine, often used in dumplings, stir-fries, and savory pancakes. They're called 'jiu cai' (韭菜) in Chinese and are one of the most important vegetables in Asian cooking!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Garlic Chives in well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water moderately, allowing the soil to dry slightly between watering. Fertilize every four weeks during the growing season. Cut leaves 2 inches above soil for continuous harvest. Both leaves and flowers are edible - the delicate white flowers have a mild garlic flavor. Divide clumps every 3-4 years.

varieties.name: Society Garlic
varieties.description: Society Garlic, botanically known as Tulbaghia violacea, is not a true chive but a related ornamental herb with narrow, strap-like leaves and a mild garlic flavor. This perennial is valued for its ornamental appeal and culinary uses. Society Garlic is known for its pretty lilac-pink flowers that bloom profusely and is suitable for both herb gardens and landscape borders.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Low to moderate - drought tolerant once established
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four to six weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate harvest of leaves and abundant flowers

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Very High - thrives in hot conditions
tolerances.cold_tolerance: Low to Moderate - hardy to zone 7-8
tolerances.drought_tolerance: High - very drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very mild garlic flavor - much milder than garlic chives, with slight onion notes

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Narrow, grass-like, blue-green leaves

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Society Garlic got its name because it was considered more 'polite' than regular garlic - it doesn't leave a strong odor on the breath! It's also a South African native and is deer and pest resistant.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Society Garlic in well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water moderately initially, then allow soil to dry between watering once established - very drought tolerant. Fertilize lightly every four to six weeks. Deadhead spent flowers to encourage more blooms. Both leaves and flowers are edible. Note: Not cold-hardy like true chives - treat as annual in cold zones or grow in containers and overwinter indoors.

varieties.name: Siberian Garlic Chives
varieties.description: Siberian Garlic Chives, also known as Blue Chives or Allium nutans, are a unique variety with distinctive blue-green foliage and nodding pink to purple flowers. This perennial herb offers a mild garlic-onion flavor and exceptional cold hardiness. Siberian Garlic Chives are prized for their ornamental beauty, culinary versatility, and ability to thrive in harsh climates where other chives might struggle.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four to six weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous harvest of leaves and edible flowers

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - tolerates heat but prefers cooler conditions
tolerances.cold_tolerance: Extremely High - hardy to zone 2-3, one of the hardiest alliums
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Moderate - somewhat drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild garlic-onion blend with slight sweetness - balanced flavor between common and garlic chives

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Flat, blue-green leaves that arch gracefully
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, flowers are ornamental and edible

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Siberian Garlic Chives are native to mountainous regions of Siberia and Central Asia, which explains their exceptional cold tolerance - they can survive temperatures well below -40°F!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Siberian Garlic Chives in well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water moderately, keeping soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four to six weeks during growing season. The attractive nodding flowers make excellent cut flowers. Harvest leaves as needed and divide clumps every 3-4 years. Excellent choice for cold-climate gardens where other varieties may not thrive.

varieties.name: Fine Leaf Chives
varieties.description: Fine Leaf Chives, also known as Fine-Leaved Chives or Slender Chives, are a delicate variety with extremely thin, thread-like leaves and a refined onion flavor. This perennial herb is prized by chefs for its elegant appearance and tender texture. Fine Leaf Chives produce abundant purple flowers and are perfect for garnishing delicate dishes where the standard chive might be too coarse or overpowering.

appearance.leaf_color: Bright Green very thin hollow tubes

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Continuous harvest - produces abundant fine foliage

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler temperatures

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very mild, delicate onion flavor - subtle and refined with sweet undertones

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Extremely slender, hollow, thread-like leaves - much finer than common chives
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, flowers are edible

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Fine Leaf Chives are a favorite in French cuisine and high-end restaurants for their delicate appearance - they're often used as 'herbes fines' and add elegance without overwhelming delicate dishes!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Fine Leaf Chives in well-drained, rich soil with full to partial sunlight. Water regularly, keeping soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support delicate growth. Harvest frequently by cutting 1-2 inches above soil level to encourage tender new growth. The fine texture makes them perfect for mincing finely as garnish. Divide clumps every 2-3 years to maintain vigor.

varieties.name: Giant Siberian Chives
varieties.description: Giant Siberian Chives are a robust, large-leaved variety with broad, flat foliage and a strong garlic flavor. This perennial herb produces the largest leaves of any chive variety, making it highly productive and valued for culinary use. Giant Siberian Chives offer exceptional cold hardiness combined with vigorous growth, producing showy white flower clusters and abundant foliage throughout the growing season.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeding every three to four weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Extremely abundant harvest - very productive variety

tolerances.heat_tolerance: High - tolerates heat well
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Moderate - somewhat drought tolerant once established

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Strong garlic flavor with robust onion undertones - more intense than standard garlic chives

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Very broad, flat leaves (up to 1 inch wide) - largest of all chive varieties
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, produces large showy flowers

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Giant Siberian Chives can produce leaves up to 3 feet tall and 1 inch wide, making them the most productive chive variety - a single clump can provide enough harvest for multiple dishes!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Giant Siberian Chives in well-drained, fertile soil with full to partial sunlight. Water regularly and fertilize every three to four weeks to support vigorous growth. Space plants generously as clumps grow very large. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage new growth. Divide large clumps every 3-4 years. Excellent for market gardeners and those wanting maximum yield from minimal space.

varieties.name: Forescate Chives
varieties.description: Forescate Chives are a unique ornamental variety bred specifically for their abundant, vibrant pink to rose-purple flowers and compact growth habit. This perennial herb produces numerous flowers over an extended period, making it valuable as both an edible ornamental and culinary herb. Forescate offers the mild onion flavor of common chives while providing exceptional visual appeal with its profuse blooms that attract pollinators.

appearance.flower_color: Vibrant Rose-Purple to Pink pom-poms (very abundant)

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light feeding every four weeks during growing season

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Moderate harvest of leaves, exceptional flower production

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - prefers cooler temperatures

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, delicate onion flavor in leaves - flowers have sweet, mild onion taste

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Slender, hollow, cylindrical leaves (similar to common chives)
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, bred for abundant flowering

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Forescate Chives can produce flowers almost continuously from late spring through fall, making them one of the longest-blooming chive varieties - perfect for edible landscaping and attracting beneficial insects!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Forescate Chives in well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water regularly, keeping soil consistently moist. Fertilize every four weeks to support abundant flowering. Deadhead spent flowers to encourage more blooms, or leave some to self-seed. Both leaves and flowers are edible. Excellent for edging beds, containers, and pollinator gardens. Divide every 2-3 years for best flowering.

varieties.name: Staro Chives
varieties.description: Staro Chives are a vigorous, high-yielding variety bred for commercial production and home gardens seeking maximum productivity. This perennial herb produces thick, uniform clumps of bright green, hollow leaves with excellent flavor and texture. Staro is valued for its rapid regrowth after cutting, disease resistance, and ability to produce abundant harvests throughout the growing season, making it a favorite among market gardeners and culinary enthusiasts.

appearance.leaf_color: Bright to Dark Green hollow tubes

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate - keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeding every three weeks during growing season for maximum production

harvest_storage.typical_yield: Extremely abundant continuous harvest - commercial-grade production

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Moderate - tolerates heat reasonably well
tolerances.drought_tolerance: Low - requires consistent moisture for best production

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Classic mild onion flavor - consistent and reliable with good intensity

herb_characteristics.leaf_texture: Uniform, hollow, cylindrical leaves with excellent texture
herb_characteristics.bolt_resistance: N/A - perennial herb, flowers are edible

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Staro Chives can be harvested up to 6-8 times per season with proper care and feeding, producing significantly more yield than standard chive varieties - making them ideal for those who use chives frequently!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Staro Chives in rich, well-drained soil with full to partial sunlight. Water regularly and fertilize every three weeks to support vigorous production. Harvest by cutting leaves 2 inches above soil level when they reach 6-8 inches tall. Plants recover quickly and produce new growth within 2 weeks. Divide clumps annually or every 2 years to maintain maximum productivity. Excellent for intensive production and commercial growing.
